findings.issue_text: [BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition interpolates a plain JS array into Prisma.sql (`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`), but Prisma raw query parameters reject plain arrays — the driver cannot bind a JS array as a single parameter, raising a query failure at runtime. Any org-scope insights query (and team-scope via userIdsFromTeam) throws when executed against the database instead of returning rows; the ANY(array) pattern in every converted condition is unusable as written.

[BUG] buildTeamAuthorizationCondition uses the same invalid `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))` array-parameter interpolation, a second instance of the unsupported raw-array binding. Team-scope insights queries fail at execution for every team with members, returning errors rather than booking data.

[ADVISORY] The public findMany method is deleted, silently breaking every existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany elsewhere in the repository, which now fail at compile time (or at runtime if JS callers exist) with no replacement path added in this diff. Any insights page/API that constructed this service and called findMany stops compiling; the diff updates only the integration test, not the production call sites.

[ADVISORY] insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema is now dead: the constructor type switched to the new hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions, leaving the exported zod schema with no runtime or type consumer, a parallel hand-maintained enumeration that will drift from the actual options type. Future schema changes (e.g. adding a scope) will update the zod schema but not the duplicate public type (or vice versa), and the next change gets riskier because two sources of truth must be kept in sync; delete the schema or type alias it.

[ADVISORY] InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions duplicates the zod-inferred InsightsBookingServiceOptions by hand and additionally loosens it (teamId? allowed on every scope, orgId required where the discriminated union may differ), so the constructor now accepts option shapes the validated schema rejects. Callers passing scope:'user' with a teamId, or shapes the zod schema was the authority on, compile fine but bypass the contract the schema encoded; the duplication is the kind that drifts on the next scope added.

[ADVISORY] The tests assert equality between two independently constructed Prisma.Sql objects via toEqual, which only passes because vitest structurally compares the internal `strings`/`values` fields of the Sql class — an implementation detail of @prisma/client, not a documented equality contract. A Prisma client upgrade that changes Sql internals (e.g. how nested values or chunk boundaries are stored) breaks every assertion in this file even when the generated SQL is identical; the next Prisma bump gets a wall of red tests that say nothing about correctness.

[BUG] The constructor's options type was changed from the zod-derived InsightsBookingServiceOptions (discriminated union where scope:"team" requires teamId) to the hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with teamId optional and no runtime zod validation, so a caller constructing the service with scope:"team" and no teamId now type-checks and reaches buildTeamAuthorizationCondition with options.teamId === undefined. Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ${undefined})` embeds an undefined parameter, so Prisma throws a parameter-binding error at query time (or produces a WHERE clause matching nothing), and the insights query for a team scope 500s instead of being rejected at construction as the discriminated-union type previously guaranteed.

[BUG] The org authorization condition interpolates the teamIds array into `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` without the length guard used for userIdsFromOrg, so when an organization has no teams (empty teamIds from findAllByParentId) the empty array parameter reaches Postgres and fails type inference. An org-owner with a teamless org gets a query error (Postgres "could not determine data type" for the empty array parameter) instead of an empty result set, crashing the insights endpoint for that user.

[ADVISORY] The public findMany method was deleted and replaced with getBaseConditions, but the exported insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema remains defined and the class is exported, so out-of-tree callers of findMany (and any code path that relied on schema.parse of options) break silently at runtime with a missing-method error rather than at compile time. Any caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany outside this diff compiles against stale types and throws TypeError at runtime; the caller migration cannot be verified from this diff, so whether this is fully migrated is unknown.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the Caching describe block (previously lines covering repeated getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions calls) even though the caching logic (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization) still exists in the service, and the only getBaseConditions test covers the both-conditions-present path, leaving the auth-only, filter-only, and no-conditions (NOTHING) combination branches in getBaseConditions with zero test coverage. A regression in the getBaseConditions else-if chain (e.g. a condition being dropped or NOTHING misapplied) or in the memoization caches goes undetected by the suite; a filter-only query silently returning NO rows (NOTHING) or all rows would ship to org owners viewing insights.

[ADVISORY] The raw SQL hardcodes physical column names ("userId", "teamId", "isTeamBooking", "eventTypeId", "eventParentId") and Postgres-specific ANY() syntax, replacing the previous Prisma field-level where-inputs that went through Prisma's field-to-column mapping and dialect abstraction. Any future @map/@@map rename or a non-Postgres deployment (SQLite/MySQL in dev/test) makes these queries fail with unknown-column errors, and the coupling is invisible to the type system; the next schema rename gets riskier because the mapping now lives in string literals scattered across five template sites.

[BUG] The public method `findMany` is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions`, silently breaking every existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`. Any in-tree or downstream caller doing `service.findMany({ select, where, ... })` now gets a TypeScript compile error at best, or at runtime a TypeError (service.findMany is not a function) — the diff contains no migration of callers, so the PR title ('convert to use Prisma.sql raw queries') does not license removing the query-executing API; the test that exercised findMany (the only consumer-facing integration test) was rewritten to call prisma.$queryRaw directly, hiding the breakage.

[ADVISORY] The zod-validated `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` is replaced as the constructor input by a hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type, discarding runtime validation of the discriminated union. A caller passing `scope: "team"` without `teamId` previously failed zod validation; now `options.teamId` is `undefined` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` interpolates `undefined` into raw SQL/queries at runtime, producing wrong authorization results instead of a validation error — an invariant the old schema enforced that this diff silently no longer enforces, and not traceable to any stated requirement of the Prisma.sql conversion.

[ADVISORY] The two Caching tests ("should cache authorization conditions", "should cache filter conditions") are deleted wholesale while the caching logic remains in the service. The memoization in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` (lines ~85-95 of insightsBooking.ts) is now completely untested; a future refactor that drops or breaks the cache (e.g., repeated DB hits per request on the hot insights path) would pass CI, and the deletion is scope drift — the PR's stated intent is a query-mechanism conversion, not test-surface reduction.

[ADVISORY] The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches in `getBaseConditions` are dead code because `getAuthorizationConditions` always returns a non-null `Prisma.Sql` (it returns NOTHING_CONDITION on every failure path). Whoever next edits this reads three reachable branches that are actually unreachable, and the final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` misleads readers into thinking an unauthenticated caller could ever reach it; the auth-conditions type should be `Prisma.Sql` (non-null) and the dead branches deleted.

[BUG] `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` produces invalid SQL because Prisma.sql flattens a JS array into a comma-separated parameter list (ANY($1, $2, $3)) instead of a single Postgres array. Any org- or team-scoped query crashes with a Postgres syntax error at or near "," at runtime; the old `teamId: { in: [...] }` Prisma where-input handled this correctly. The new integration tests only compare the Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual and never execute the ANY branches, so CI stays green while org/team insights are broken in production.

[BUG] An organization with zero child teams (or an empty userIdsFromOrg combined with empty teamIds) yields `("teamId" = ANY())` with zero parameters, which is a Postgres syntax error. An org owner of a freshly created org (no teams, no members) opening insights gets a 500 from a syntax error, whereas the old `teamId: { in: [] }` where-input was a well-formed always-false condition; org scope's unconditional first condition makes this reachable for every empty org.

[BUG] The public method `findMany` was removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`, a breaking change to the service's API surface with no compat shim or versioning. Every existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (routes/insights endpoints outside this diff) now fails to compile at build time, and any caller migrated by hand-writing raw SQL loses the soft-delete/tenant scoping the Prisma where-input previously guaranteed; callers must now know the physical table name "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" and its quoting rules.

[ADVISORY] A second, hand-maintained option type `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` now shadows the existing zod schema `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema`, and the two already disagree: the public type requires `orgId: number` for every scope while the zod discriminated union is the previous source of truth. The zod schema is now dead validation that will silently drift from the constructor type; a future scope/field change updates one copy and not the other, and runtime validation of options (bad scope strings, wrong shapes) is gone entirely since nothing parses the schema anymore.

[ADVISORY] Column and table identifiers ("userId", "teamId", "isTeamBooking", "eventTypeId") are duplicated as raw quoted strings across the service and its tests instead of shared constants, so a Prisma schema field rename changes semantics for neither TypeScript nor Prisma's type-checked where-inputs. The next schema rename (e.g. userId -> ownerId) compiles clean everywhere and produces a runtime `column does not exist` error only in production queries; the same duplication in tests means expectations track the service's typos rather than the schema.

[BUG] The public query method findMany was deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions, which returns a raw SQL fragment instead of running the query, silently breaking every existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany at compile time and forcing all call sites to hand-write $queryRaw against BookingTimeStatusDenormalized. Any existing controller/route calling service.findMany({select, ...}) now fails to compile (or, after refactoring callers, must re-implement select/pagination/where-merging that findMany previously handled), and nothing in the diff shows explicit human acceptance of removing this public API — the diff itself has no caller migration.

[BUG] The constructor's options type changed from the zod-validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions (which requires teamId for scope:'team') to the unvalidated InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions where teamId is optional, so buildTeamAuthorizationCondition at line ~185 runs with options.teamId === undefined. A caller passing {scope:'team', userId, orgId} without teamId (previously rejected by the zod schema at the type level and by validation) now reaches Prisma.sql`"teamId" = ${undefined}`, producing a PrismaClientValidationError or a query with a null/undefined bound parameter that silently matches no rows — runtime validation of options was dropped without acceptance, converting a fail-fast contract into silent misbehavior.

[ADVISORY] insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema remains exported but is no longer applied to constructor input, leaving a ships-inert validator whose shape and the new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type can drift independently (two parallel sources of truth for the same options contract). The next contributor editing the zod schema to add/change a field (e.g. making teamId conditional) sees no type error because nothing consumes the schema for validation, and the shipped type silently diverges; also runtime validation of attacker-influenced inputs on the insights route disappears.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes both caching tests ('should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions') while the caching behavior (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization) remains in the service at insightsBooking.ts lines ~87-97, leaving that behavior with zero coverage. A regression in the memoization (e.g. someone removing the cache or making it cache incorrectly across option changes) passes the entire integration suite; caching is performance-bearing on the insights endpoint and its loss would only surface as slow queries in production.

[ADVISORY] The constructor now accepts the hand-written InsightsBookingPublicOptions type instead of parsing through insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema, so the zod validation that previously enforced the discriminated-union shape (and required teamId for scope:"team") is no longer applied at this entry point. Any caller passing malformed options (e.g. scope "team" without teamId, or non-numeric userId from an unvalidated request payload) gets scope-dependent behavior instead of a parse-time rejection — buildTeamAuthorizationCondition would run teamRepo.findByIdAndParentId with undefined id, silently falling through to NOTHING_CONDITION or unexpected scoping; parameterization prevents SQL injection, but the trust-boundary hardening that the schema provided is gone, and the next caller who assumes validated input gets bitten.

[BUG] expect(conditions).toEqual(NOTHING_CONDITION) cannot distinguish conditions from any other Prisma.Sql instance, because Prisma.Sql stores its SQL fragments and values in private class fields (#prismaSqlValues/#prismaSqlText) that vitest's toEqual structural comparison cannot see, so the assertion passes for literally any Sql the service returns. If buildAuthorizationConditions regressed to return e.g. Prisma.sql`1=1` (a full-data-leak condition) instead of 1=0, the 'unauthorized user gets nothing' tests still pass green, giving false confidence that the authorization deny path is verified.

[BUG] The rewritten condition assertions (e.g. expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`)) compare two Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual, which sees no own enumerable properties on Sql and therefore passes regardless of the actual SQL text and parameter values the service built. Every SQL-shape regression in buildAuthorizationConditions/buildFilterConditions — wrong column name, inverted isTeamBooking polarity, missing teamId IS NULL — goes undetected; the suite reports green while shipping broken authorization SQL to production.

[ADVISORY] The caching tests ('should cache authorization conditions', 'should cache filter conditions') were deleted entirely, yet the caching behavior remains in the service (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts:81-93), leaving the cache-hit branches with zero test coverage in this diff. A future refactor that drops or mis-keys the condition caches (e.g. returning stale conditions across filter changes) ships with no failing test; the next maintainer loses the regression net the old suite had.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions has four branches (both conditions, auth-only, filter-only, neither->NOTHING_CONDITION) but the only test in the diff that exercises it (integration-test ~line 477) covers just the both-conditions path, leaving the auth-only, filter-only, and NOTHING fall-through branches untested. A regression in the reduce/branching logic — e.g. the else-if chain returning filterConditions when authConditions is null, silently bypassing authorization — passes the full suite because no test ever queries with filters but no membership or with a scope that yields auth-only.

[ADVISORY] The only test that executes the generated SQL against a real database ($queryRaw in the getBaseConditions test) exercises a single user booking, so the ANY(array) parameterization path — which Prisma.sql expands arrays into comma-separated parameter lists ($1, $2), producing `= ANY($1, $2)` that is invalid in a single-argument ANY() — is never executed with a multi-element array despite three tests constructing multi-element expectations (org test lines ~329-340, team arrays). If Prisma's array expansion makes `"userId" = ANY(${[a,b]})` invalid SQL, org- and team-scope insights queries with more than one member fail at runtime in production while every test in this diff stays green, because the multi-value ANY conditions are only compared structurally (tautologically) and never run.

[BUG] Interpolating a plain JS array inside Prisma.sql ("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) throws at runtime, because Prisma's Sql template tag rejects arrays — lists must be wrapped in Prisma.join(). buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition throw a PrismaClientValidationError the first time an org/team scope insights query runs with a non-empty team/user list, so org and team insights pages 500 while user scope keeps working — the failure surfaces only on the paths the diff's user-scope happy path never exercises.

[ADVISORY] The constructor now accepts InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (with teamId optional) instead of the zod-validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions, dropping the schema that previously constrained inputs, while buildTeamAuthorizationCondition dereferences options.teamId unconditionally. A caller constructing the service with scope: "team" and no teamId compiles cleanly under the new type and produces Prisma.sql`"teamId" = ${undefined}`, which throws a raw-query parameter error (or, if teamId arrives as null, matches no rows) — the type widening converts a previously schema-caught mistake into a runtime SQL failure.

[ADVISORY] The public findMany method is deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions, silently changing the service's exported surface while keeping the class name and constructor intact. Any out-of-tree or sibling callers of InsightsBookingService.findMany (which previously received fully-formed, Prisma-typed rows with select support) now fail at runtime with a missing-method error or must hand-roll $queryRaw with the same table/column naming; nothing in the diff updates consumers beyond the test file, so a caller missed in the grep-based sweep ships broken.

[BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition interpolates a possibly-empty JS array into `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`, and Prisma serializes an empty array parameter as an untyped/empty Postgres array, producing `operator does not exist: integer = text[]` on the raw query. An org owner/admin of an org with zero child teams (or whose child teams have no members) calling the insights endpoint gets a raw Postgres error / 500 from the raw query instead of an empty result set; previously the Prisma `in: []` where-clause safely returned no rows.

[ADVISORY] The constructor now accepts InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions directly while insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema is no longer used to validate input at construction, and the `scope` else-branch silently maps any invalid scope string to NOTHING_CONDITION. A caller passing a mistyped scope (e.g. `"organisation"`) gets a silently empty insights result reported as success (no rows, no error, no log), which is indistinguishable from legitimate zero-data and misdirects debugging toward data issues; only the integration tests exercise valid scopes.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions hands callers a raw Prisma.Sql fragment that is only valid against the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table and only inside a WHERE clause, replacing the previous type-safe findMany boundary with an untyped SQL string contract. Any future caller that interpolates the fragment against a different table, into a non-WHERE position, or with user-controlled additional SQL gets a runtime Postgres syntax/42883 error (or worse) with no compile-time signal — the next change to this service gets riskier because the safety formerly enforced by Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput is gone.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition interpolates a plain JS array into Prisma.sql (`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`), but Prisma raw query parameters reject plain arrays — the driver cannot bind a JS array as a single parameter, raising a query failure at runtime. Any org-scope insights query (and team-scope via userIdsFromTeam) throws when executed against the database instead of returning rows; the ANY(array) pattern in every converted condition is unusable as written.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does interpolate JS number arrays into `Prisma.sql` and uses them with Postgres `ANY(...)` (e.g. `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`` and similarly for user IDs). However, the finding’s core claim—"Prisma raw query parameters reject plain arrays" and will "throw at runtime"—is not verifiable from the diff. Nothing in the diff demonstrates such a failure, and using `ANY($1)` with an array parameter is a valid SQL pattern on Postgres (as opposed to `IN (${array})`, which would indeed be wrong). Therefore the asserted guaranteed runtime failure is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] buildTeamAuthorizationCondition uses the same invalid `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))` array-parameter interpolation, a second instance of the unsupported raw-array binding. Team-scope insights queries fail at execution for every team with members, returning errors rather than booking data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` constructing `Prisma.sql` with `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))`, but nothing in the diff demonstrates that binding a `number[]` this way is “unsupported” or that it will fail at execution. The same `ANY(${...})` pattern is also used in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and in updated integration test expectations, and the diff contains no evidence (errors, guards, or comments) that this interpolation is invalid. The claim that team-scope queries will error for any team with members is therefore not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the public `findMany(...)` method from `InsightsBookingService` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` (see `insightsBooking.ts`). The integration test is updated to use `getBaseConditions` + `$queryRaw`, but the diff does not show any production call sites being updated. If other parts of the repo still call `service.findMany(...)`, this change will break them at compile time (TS) or runtime (JS). The claim that it breaks “every existing caller elsewhere in the repository” can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the API break risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` and changes the `InsightsBookingService` constructor to accept that (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`), while the existing `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` and `InsightsBookingServiceOptions = z.infer<typeof ...>` remain in the file. Even if the schema/type are still referenced internally (e.g., `private options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null;` and method signatures using `Extract<InsightsBookingServiceOptions, ...>`), the constructor no longer uses the zod-derived type and does no runtime validation, creating two parallel sources of truth (notably `teamId?: number` in the new public type vs the schema’s likely-required `teamId` for `scope: "team"`). This is a concrete maintainability/consistency risk introduced by the change, though the claim that the schema has *no* type consumer cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` as the constructor parameter type (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`), but the service still validates with `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse(options)` and stores `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. Since `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` is a hand-written, looser shape (notably `teamId?: number` on all scopes), TypeScript will now allow calls like `{ scope: "team", teamId: undefined }` or `{ scope: "user", teamId: 123 }` to compile even though the zod discriminated union is likely stricter. Those calls will then fail at runtime during `parse`, turning what used to be a compile-time error into a runtime exception. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and can break callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes tests to assert `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` in multiple places (e.g. `getAuthorizationConditions`, `getFilterConditions`, and `getBaseConditions`). This compares two separately constructed `Prisma.Sql` instances for deep structural equality rather than asserting on behavior (e.g., executing the condition or normalizing the rendered SQL). That makes the tests tightly coupled to `Prisma.Sql`’s internal shape (whatever fields vitest deep-compares), so a Prisma upgrade that changes how `Sql` stores `strings`/`values` or nests chunks could break these assertions even if the resulting SQL semantics are unchanged. This is a concrete fragility introduced by the diff, but it’s about test robustness rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the constructor parameter type to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, but the class still stores `private options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null;` (the zod-derived discriminated union). For this to type-check, the constructor must still be parsing/validating `options` into `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (as it did previously), which would reject `{ scope: "team" }` without `teamId` at construction time. The finding’s claim that there is “no runtime zod validation” and that `options.teamId === undefined` reaches `Prisma.sql` is not supported by what’s shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The org authorization condition interpolates the teamIds array into `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` without the length guard used for userIdsFromOrg, so when an organization has no teams (empty teamIds from findAllByParentId) the empty array parameter reaches Postgres and fails type inference. An org-owner with a teamless org gets a query error (Postgres "could not determine data type" for the empty array parameter) instead of an empty result set, crashing the insights endpoint for that user.

adjudication.rationale: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the code always creates an OR branch with `Prisma.sql` using `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)` even when `teamIds` is an empty array (derived from `teamsFromOrg.map(...)`). Unlike `userIdsFromOrg`, there is no empty-length guard. This diff replaces Prisma's `in: teamIds` (which safely handles empty arrays) with a raw `ANY($1)` parameter, and with an empty array parameter Postgres can error due to ambiguous/unknown array type unless explicitly cast. Thus a teamless org can trigger a query error instead of returning no rows.

If there are any callers elsewhere (not shown in this diff) still invoking `service.findMany(...)`, they will break and need migration.
